title: Point blowup lowers intersection multiplicity of regular curves
statement: Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme and let $Y,Z\subseteq X$ be closed subschemes. Suppose $Y$ is integral of dimension $1$, $p\in Y\cap Z$ is closed, $\mathcal O_{Y,p}$ is regular, and the generic point of $Y$ is not in $Z$. Define $m_p(Y,Z)=\operatorname{length}_{\mathcal O_{X,p}}(\mathcal O_{Y\cap Z,p})$, with scheme-theoretic intersection cut out by the sum of the ideals. This is a positive finite integer. Blow up $p$, writing $Y',Z'$ for strict transforms and $E$ for the exceptional divisor. Then $Y'\to Y$ is an isomorphism; $Y'\cap E$ consists of a single point $q$, with $m_q(Y',E)=1$; and if $q\in Z'$, then $m_q(Y',Z')<m_p(Y,Z)$. Conventions: [pqf-def-locnoeth], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-weil-closed-immersion], [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], [def-weil-regular-scheme], [def-sc-generic-point], [def-nagata-global-blowup], [def-nagata-strict-transform], [def-weil-pbc-module-length].

source.place: Stacks Project Tag 0BI7 (resolve-lemma-blowup-nonsingular-curves-meeting-at-point), using the local uniformizer calculation and valuation drop.

proof.text: Put $S=\mathcal O_{X,p}$ and $R=\mathcal O_{Y,p}$. The closed immersion gives a surjection $S\to R$. The ring $R$ is Noetherian and a domain. Its dimension is one: the generic point of the integral one-dimensional $Y$ is distinct from its closed point $p$, giving a chain of length one, and a longer chain in the local spectrum would give a longer chain in $Y$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-dim-one-iff-normal] to the assumed regular local ring $R$, and then [lem-sc-normal-dim1-dvr], to obtain a DVR. In particular every ideal of $R$ is principal, and its maximal ideal has a nonzero generator $\tau$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring].

Lift $\tau$ to an element $t$ of the maximal ideal of $S$. Represent it on an affine Noetherian neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $p$, with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ and ideals $I,J$ for $Y,Z$. Write $B=A/I$. After replacing $U$ by a smaller principal neighbourhood of $p$, we have $\mathfrak m=I+(t)$: choose finite generators of $\mathfrak m$; their classes in $R=B_{\mathfrak m/I}$ are multiples of $\tau$, and clear the finitely many denominators and the finitely many equalities. Thus the ideal of the reduced point $p$ on $Y\cap U$ is $(\bar t)$. Since $B$ is a domain and $\bar t\ne0$, this is a free ideal of rank one. Away from $p$ the ideal of $p$ is the unit ideal. Hence that ideal is invertible on all of $Y$ [def-nagata-invertible-ideal].

proof.text: Apply [thm-nagata-strict-transform-is-blowup] to the closed immersion $Y\to X$ and the ideal of $p$. It identifies $Y^\prime$ over $Y$ with the blowup of the invertible ideal just obtained. By [cor-nagata-blowup-cartier-iso], $Y^\prime\to Y$ is an isomorphism. The exceptional divisor is defined by the extended centre ideal, which is an effective Cartier ideal by [thm-nagata-blowup-principalizes-center]. Its intersection with $Y^\prime$ is therefore the inverse image of the reduced closed point $p\subset Y$; in particular its underlying set is a single point, denoted $q$.

source.place: Tag 0BI7, lemma-blowup-nonsingular-curves-meeting-at-point, proof, Cartier centre and strict-transform identification

proof.text: Let $H=JR\subset R$. This is nonzero because the generic point of $Y$ is not in $Z$, and is proper because $p\in Z$. Since $R$ is a DVR, write $H=(a)$ with $a\ne0$. We may choose $a$ to be the image of an element $f\in J$: express any generator as a finite $R$-linear combination of images of elements of $J$, and clear its denominators in $B\setminus(\mathfrak m/I)$; the resulting multiplier is a unit in $R$. Then $a\in\tau R$. The finite-length lemma [lem-weil-pbc-dim-le-one-principal-quotient-finite-length] applies to this nonzerodivisor $a$ in the Noetherian ring $R$ of dimension one. Thus $R/(a)$ has positive finite length. Its $S$-submodules and $R$-submodules are identical, since $S\to R$ is surjective; consequently this length is precisely $m=m_p(Y,Z)$ by [def-weil-pbc-module-length].

proof.text: Use the $t$-chart $\operatorname{Spec}C$ of the blowup over $U$, where $C=A[\mathfrak m/t]$ [prop-nagata-affine-blowup-chart, def-nagata-affine-blowup-chart-map, def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring]. The global blowup restricts over $U$ to the affine local model $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathfrak m}(U)$: by [prop-nagata-global-blowup-cover-independent] the open immersion $\iota_U$ identifies it with the preimage of $U$ over $U$ [def-nagata-global-blowup, def-nagata-global-blowup-glue-data, def-nagata-global-blowup-local-model]. Define $\psi:C\to B$ by $y/t^n\mapsto\bar y/\bar t^n$ for $y\in\mathfrak m^n$. This lies in $B$ because $\mathfrak m^nB=(\bar t^n)$. Equality of two fractions can be multiplied by a power of $t$; reducing modulo $I$ and cancelling the nonzero element $\bar t$ proves that $\psi$ is well defined. The same cancellation verifies addition and multiplication. The resulting map $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}C$ factors through $Y^\prime$: every equation of the scheme-theoretic closure vanishes after inverting $\bar t$ and hence vanishes in the domain $B$ [def-nagata-strict-transform, def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image]. Its composite to $Y\cap U$ is the identity. By the isomorphism in step 3 it is the inverse on this neighbourhood. In particular $q$ lies on this chart and $\mathcal O_{Y^\prime,q}=R$.

proof.text: On this chart the ideal of $E$ is $\mathfrak m C$ [lemma-nagata-extended-ideal-affine-chart], and $\mathfrak m C=(t)$ [lemma-nagata-chart-extended-ideal-principal]: the inclusion $(t)\subseteq\mathfrak m C$ holds since $t\in\mathfrak m$, and every generator $y\in\mathfrak m$ equals $t(y/t)$. Under $\psi$ this ideal becomes $(\bar t)$ and at $q$ becomes $(\tau)$. Thus the intersection stalk is $R/\tau R$, its residue field. This module has just two submodules and hence length one [def-weil-pbc-module-length]. The closed immersion gives a surjection $\mathcal O_{X^\prime,q}\to R$, so its submodules over the ambient stalk are the same; therefore $m_q(Y^\prime,E)=1$.

Let $L\subset C$ be the ideal of $Z^\prime$ on the chosen chart. Away from $E$ the chart is $D(t)$, and the restriction of $Z^\prime$ there is defined by $JC_t$. The closure definition says that its ideal is $L=\ker(C\to(C/JC)_t)$ [def-nagata-strict-transform, def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image]. Since $f\in J\subset\mathfrak m$, the element $f/t\in C$ maps to zero in this localization, and therefore belongs to $L$. Its image in $R$ is $b=a/\tau$, which is nonzero. Let $K=\psi(L)R$; then $(b)\subseteq K$, and $R/K$ is the intersection stalk at $q$. If $q\in Z^\prime$, the ideal $K$ is proper.

source.place: Tag 0BI7, lemma-blowup-nonsingular-curves-meeting-at-point, proof, inclusion of f/x_1 in the strict-transform ideal

proof.text: Assume $q\in Z^\prime$. Multiplication by $\tau$ identifies $R/(b)$ with the proper submodule $\tau R/(a)$ of $R/(a)$: it is injective because $\tau$ is nonzero in the domain $R$, and $a=\tau b$. It is proper because its quotient is the nonzero field $R/\tau R$. Every strict submodule chain in $R/K$ pulls back under the surjection $R/(b)\to R/K$ to a strict chain in $R/(b)$, and hence in $\tau R/(a)$; appending the larger module $R/(a)$ adds one strict inclusion. By the definition of length [def-weil-pbc-module-length], $\operatorname{length}_R(R/K)+1\le m$. This also proves that $R/K$ has finite length. Since $\mathcal O_{X^\prime,q}\to R$ is surjective, its module length over that ambient stalk equals its length over $R$. We obtain $m_q(Y^\prime,Z^\prime)<m_p(Y,Z)$, as required. If $b$ is a unit then $K=R$, so the conditional case cannot occur; this includes the transverse case $m=1$.
